intake_records.subject: 2026-09-04 external tooling intake — GitHub MCP, deterministic video, malware sandboxes, design/render services
intake_records.instruction_ref: Owner message 2026-09-04: remember/save findings; review GitHub MCP Server, auto-video-gen, ANY.RUN, Hybrid Analysis, Fabrie, ReRender AI, mnml.ai, LookX AI, PromeAI, Midjourney, Equimake; preserve free-first and minimal-user-action policy.
intake_records.scope: Research-only intake. (1) GitHub MCP Server: official GitHub remote/local MCP, toolsets/read-only/lockdown; candidate provider-neutral GitHub adapter where a host lacks equivalent native GitHub tools; do not duplicate working native connectors. (2) Cuongyd196/auto-video-gen: MIT, Node/TypeScript + HyperFrames + Edge TTS + FFmpeg deterministic short-form pipeline; potentially useful for P2P post-production, recap/trailer/Tier C-D hybrid video, but exact execution in Arena is not yet proven because HyperFrames requires Chrome/Chromium. (3) ANY.RUN and Hybrid Analysis: external untrusted-artifact/malware triage only; public/free submissions can expose uploaded samples, so never submit secrets, confidential builds, or private P2P artifacts; not general-purpose compute sandboxes. (4) Fabrie/ReRender/mnml.ai/LookX/PromeAI/Midjourney/Equimake: research-only visual/design tools. ReRender/mnml/LookX/PromeAI may be useful for beauty-reference or architecture/location experiments; free tiers/API/commercial rights vary and must remain TEMPORARY_RESOURCE unless proven. Midjourney is paid on web/Discord and does not provide general authorized automation/API; not a free-first renderer. Equimake offers free browser 3D experiences/GLTF export and may be useful for lightweight collaborative 3D presentation, not a render-compute substitute. (5) Owner UX rule: prefer API/CLI automation and minimal user actions; if stronger free sandbox/GPU is needed, Control Tower should choose one justified provider and give beginner-safe step-by-step setup rather than asking Owner to compare technical options.
intake_records.machinery_rule: Research-only means no vendoring, no new router/orchestrator, no credentials, no paid dependency, and no runtime claim without a bounded execution proof. Prefer exact pinned upstream execution or a thin provider-neutral adapter. Existing native capabilities take precedence over installing duplicate infrastructure.

intake_records.subject: Google Colab MCP — local-agent bridge to browser Colab session
intake_records.scope: Official googlecolab/colab-mcp (main pin b9ab3899e0f1fa493390b1fd6d54aa2e464ecdf1, package 1.0.1, Apache-2.0). It runs an MCP server on the user's local machine, opens a Google Colab browser tab, and bridges the MCP client to tools exposed by that Colab frontend over an authenticated localhost WebSocket. Requires an MCP client that supports notifications/tools/list_changed and runs locally; README names Gemini CLI, Claude Code, and Windsurf. It is NOT a remote Colab API and cannot directly be used by Arena's remote sandbox, because the Colab page connects back to localhost on the user's device. Candidate value for P2P: reduce Owner actions after one-time local setup by letting a supported local agent operate Colab notebooks/runtime instead of manual upload/Run all. Potentially useful for free GPU/network escape-hatch workflows, including IMAGE_BRIDGE, but exact notebook/runtime/GPU control exposed by the live Colab frontend must be bounded-proofed before claiming automation. Do not build a second Colab controller; use exact upstream MCP if adopted.
intake_records.machinery_rule: Treat as a LOCAL_EXECUTION_ADAPTER, not a cloud service or Arena capability. No credential storage or remote tunnelling should be added merely to force Arena compatibility. Prefer one bounded proof on the Owner's Windows machine using one supported local MCP client; only after proof may it replace manual Colab steps.
